title: Exploring the Influence of Students' Modes of Behavioral Engagement in an Online Programming Course Using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling
reason: Re-extraction. OpenEdu/LMS log constructs (online days, video-watching events, document reading) and in-platform self-assessment scores related to final grade by PLS-SEM, n = 217. Path coefficients and R2 reported; Table 2 n, country and effect cells can be filled.

extraction.design: PLS-SEM on log data (direct, indirect effects, IPMA)
extraction.n_quote: we analyzed the log data of 217 students.
extraction.population: undergraduates in an online Python programming course (82% information engineering/computer science majors), 1 university, spring 2021
extraction.lms_indicators: Online_days (days with log activity); video-watching events (load, play, pause, seek backward, stop, etc.); online document reading; self-assessment scores from Game_test, OJ_test, Unit_test

effect_sizes.between: in-platform self-assessment scores (activity products) ↔ final grade

extraction.notes: Table 2 changes: country Taiwan (not nr), n = 217 (not nr), effect sizes available (largest log-to-grade direct path 0.113 for video watching; R2 = 0.771 is dominated by self-assessment scores, path 0.819). Document reading paths n.s. (-0.018, 0.037). Design is PLS-SEM on log constructs, not clustering: Table 2's '(behavioural-engagement clusters)' and the manuscript's 'cluster modes ... inferring learning strategies' do not match; no learning-strategy or personality construct is measured. 15 of 28 log indicators dropped for low loadings. 315 registered, 217 with log data.
